DDD · Value Objects · Clean Architecture A production-grade e-commerce engine built on clean architecture — from value objects and aggregate roots to repositories and application services. Complete with live, interactive code examples you can run in your browser. This guide walks you through every component of a real-world shopping cart system using Domain-Driven Design (DDD) principles. You'll learn how to model money safely, enforce business invariants, and build a system that's ready for a REST API or database layer. 📅 July 15, 2026 ⏱ 20 min read 🎓 Intermediate 🐍 Python 3.9+ 11Code Components 6DDD Patterns ₱PHP Support ▶Run in Browser Back to Abstraction Guide 01 — The Foundation This project demonstrates how to build a real-world e-commerce shopping cart in Python using Domain-Driven Design (DDD) — an architectural approach that puts business logic at the heart of your codebase. Unlike tutorial-grade CRUD apps, this system mirrors how large platforms structure their backend services. The cart handles currency-safe arithmetic, inventory management, order placement, and a full interactive CLI — all without a single external framework. Every code example in this guide is fully interactive — you can copy and run each snippet right in your browser using the Pyodide Python runtime. No setup required. 6 DDD patterns explained 11 code components 5 knowledge-check questions Live code runner Real-world extensions Junior developers — understand how real software is structured beyond tutorials Intermediate Pythonistas — see @dataclass, Decimal, uuid, datetime used together CS students — study applied OOP: encapsulation, abstraction, SOLID Backend engineers — a reference implementation for e-commerce domain models Tech educators — a production-pattern example to teach from Domain Layer — Money, Product, CartItem, ShoppingCart, Order, Address Repository Layer — InMemoryProductRepository, InMemoryOrderRepository Application Layer — place_order() service function Presentation Layer — interactive CLI in main() 💡 Layer Separation: Each layer has one responsibility. Swapping the CLI for a REST API requires touching only the presentation layer — the domain stays untouched. 02 — Component Breakdown A component-by-component breakdown of the system's most important pieces. from dataclasses import dataclass from decimal import Decimal from typing import Union @dataclass(frozen=True) class Money: amount: Decimal currency: str = "PHP" def __add__(self, other: 'Money') -> 'Money': if not isinstance(other, Money): return NotImplemented if self.currency != other.currency: raise ValueError("Cannot add different currencies") return Money(self.amount + other.amount, self.currency) def __mul__(self, quantity: Union[int, float, Decimal]) -> 'Money': if isinstance(quantity, float): quantity = Decimal(str(quantity)) elif isinstance(quantity, int): quantity = Decimal(quantity) return Money(self.amount * quantity, self.currency) def __str__(self) -> str: if self.currency == "PHP": return f"₱{self.amount:,.2f}" return f"{self.amount:,.2f} {self.currency}" 📝 Why This Matters Why Decimal? Using floats for money leads to rounding errors — 0.1 + 0.2 ≠ 0.3. Decimal provides exact decimal arithmetic. Why frozen=True? Money is a value object — it should be immutable. Two instances with the same amount and currency are interchangeable. Freezing prevents mutation and makes it hashable. Safe Arithmetic: __add__ validates currency compatibility and returns a new Money instance. __mul__ safely converts types before multiplying. Localized Formatting: __str__ adds the ₱ symbol and thousand separators for Philippine Peso display. @dataclass class Product: id: str name: str description: str price: Money sku: str stock_quantity: int = 0 def has_stock(self, qty: int = 1) -> bool: return self.stock_quantity >= qty def reduce_stock(self, qty: int) -> None: if qty <= 0: raise ValueError("Quantity to reduce must be positive") if not self.has_stock(qty): raise ValueError(f"Insufficient stock for {self.name}") self.stock_quantity -= qty 📝 Why This Matters Entity vs Value Object: Products have an identity (id) and mutable state (stock) — they are entities, not value objects. Inventory Logic in the Domain: has_stock and reduce_stock centralise business rules, preventing negative stock anywhere in the system. Invariant Enforcement: Both methods raise descriptive ValueError exceptions on violation — keeping error handling explicit and domain-driven. class ShoppingCart: def __init__(self, cart_id: str = None): self.id = cart_id or str(uuid.uuid4()) self.items: Dict[str, CartItem] = {} self.created_at = datetime.now() self.updated_at = self.created_at def add_item(self, product: Product, quantity: int = 1) -> None: if quantity <= 0: return if not product.has_stock(quantity): raise ValueError(f"Not enough stock for {product.name}") if product.id in self.items: current = self.items[product.id] new_qty = current.quantity + quantity if not product.has_stock(new_qty): raise ValueError(f"Not enough stock for {product.name}") self.items[product.id] = CartItem( product=product, quantity=new_qty, added_at=current.added_at ) else: self.items[product.id] = CartItem( product=product, quantity=quantity, added_at=datetime.now() ) self.updated_at = datetime.now() @property def total(self) -> Money: if not self.items: return Money(Decimal(0)) total = Money(Decimal(0)) for item in self.items.values(): total += item.subtotal return total 📝 Why This Matters What is an Aggregate Root? The cart is the entry point that enforces consistency rules for all its items. It guarantees that adding an item never exceeds available stock. O(1) Lookups: Using a dictionary keyed by product ID makes lookups fast and naturally merges duplicate additions. Computed Total: The total property is computed on-demand using safe Money arithmetic — always accurate without manual recalculation. Timestamps: created_at and updated_at enable audit logs and debugging. 03 — Full Source Code Copy and save as shopping_cart.py — or Run it directly in your browser. python · shopping_cart.py Copy Run float): quantity = Decimal(str(quantity)) elif isinstance(quantity, int): quantity = Decimal(quantity) return Money(self.amount * quantity, self.currency) def __str__(self) -> str: if self.currency == "PHP": return f"₱{self.amount:,.2f}" return f"{self.amount:,.2f} {self.currency}" @dataclass class Product: id: str name: str description: str price: Money sku: str stock_quantity: int = 0 def has_stock(self, qty: int = 1) -> bool: return self.stock_quantity >= qty def reduce_stock(self, qty: int) -> None: if qty <= 0: raise ValueError("Quantity to reduce must be positive") if not self.has_stock(qty): raise ValueError(f"Insufficient stock for {self.name}") self.stock_quantity -= qty @dataclass class CartItem: product: Product quantity: int added_at: datetime = field(default_factory=datetime.now) @property def subtotal(self) -> Money: return self.product.price * self.quantity class ShoppingCart: def __init__(self, cart_id: str = None): self.id = cart_id or str(uuid.uuid4()) self.items: Dict[str, CartItem] = {} self.created_at = datetime.now() self.updated_at = self.created_at def add_item(self, product: Product, quantity: int = 1) -> None: if quantity <= 0: return if not product.has_stock(quantity): raise ValueError(f"Not enough stock for {product.name}") if product.id in self.items: current = self.items[product.id] new_qty = current.quantity + quantity if not product.has_stock(new_qty): raise ValueError(f"Not enough stock for {product.name}") self.items[product.id] = CartItem( product=product, quantity=new_qty, added_at=current.added_at ) else: self.items[product.id] = CartItem( product=product, quantity=quantity, added_at=datetime.now() ) self.updated_at = datetime.now() def remove_item(self, product_id: str) -> None: if product_id in self.items: del self.items[product_id] self.updated_at = datetime.now() def clear(self) -> None: self.items.clear() self.updated_at = datetime.now() @property def total(self) -> Money: if not self.items: return Money(Decimal(0)) total = Money(Decimal(0)) for item in self.items.values(): total += item.subtotal return total def __repr__(self) -> str: return f"ShoppingCart(id={self.id!r}, items={len(self.items)}, total={self.total})" class InMemoryCartRepository: def __init__(self): self._store: Dict[str, ShoppingCart] = {} def save(self, cart: ShoppingCart) -> None: self._store[cart.id] = cart def find_by_id(self, cart_id: str) -> ShoppingCart | None: return self._store.get(cart_id) def delete(self, cart_id: str) -> None: self._store.pop(cart_id, None) if ShoppingCart() repo = InMemoryCartRepository() print(f"
Cart ID : {cart.id}") print(f"Total : {cart.total} (empty cart)

Repository round-trip OK: {loaded is cart}") print("
Testing domain invariants...") try: cart.add_item(laptop, 999) except ValueError as e: print(f" ✅ Caught expected error: {e}") try: laptop.reduce_stock(-1) except ValueError as e: print(f" ✅ Caught expected error: {e}") print("
Done.") 04 — DDD Concepts Reference Quick-reference guide to the patterns used in this system. ConceptClassTypeKey Responsibility MoneyValue ObjectImmutableSafe decimal arithmetic with currency awareness ProductEntityMutableProduct identity + inventory management CartItemValue ObjectImmutableA line-item snapshot within the cart ShoppingCartAggregate RootControllerEnforces all cart business invariants OrderEntityMutableOrder lifecycle tracking InMemoryCartRepositoryRepositoryStoragePersist and query carts (swappable with DB) 05 — Best Practices 🔢 Always use Decimal for money — Python's float cannot represent all decimal fractions exactly. Initialize with strings: Decimal("19.99") not Decimal(19.99). 🧊 Freeze your value objects — Use @dataclass(frozen=True) on value objects like Money. This makes them hashable and prevents accidental mutation. 🏗 Push logic into the domain — Business rules belong in the domain entity, not in a controller. Domain objects should validate their own invariants and raise exceptions on violation. 🔑 Use UUIDs for identity — Generate IDs with str(uuid.uuid4()). UUIDs are globally unique and make distributed systems simpler. 📦 Repository pattern = swappable storage — Your in-memory repository can be replaced with SQLAlchemy, MongoDB, or Firebase without touching domain code. 🔄 Timestamps on every mutation — Store created_at and updated_at on mutable entities for audit logs and debugging. 06 — Learning Roadmap Follow this progression to master Python e-commerce architecture step by step. Before diving into DDD, ensure you're comfortable with Python classes, @dataclass, type hints, and exception handling. These are the grammar of domain models. See how well you understood the patterns. ✅ Submit Quiz 🔄 Reset 0/5 Great effort — review any missed questions above. ↺ Retry Quiz 08 — Bad Code vs Clean Code See exactly how DDD patterns improve naive Python approaches — side by side. ❌ Naive Approach (Float Money) price = 19.99 qty = 3 total = price * qty # Result: 59.97000000000001 ❌ tax = total * 0.12 grand = total + tax print(f"Total: {grand:.2f}") # Fragile, loses precision ✅ DDD Value Object (Decimal Money) price = Money(Decimal("19.99")) qty = 3 total = price * qty # Result: ₱59.97 ✅ tax = total * Decimal("0.12") grand = total + tax print(grand) # ₱67.17 # Precise, safe, readable ❌ Logic Scattered in Script stock = 5 ordered = 10 # Validation scattered everywhere: if ordered > stock: print("No stock") # No central enforcement # Bug: easy to bypass check ✅ Invariant in Domain Entity product.reduce_stock(qty) # raises ValueError automatically # if insufficient stock. # Rules live in ONE place — # impossible to bypass or forget. # Domain is always consistent. 💡 Key insight: Moving validation into domain objects means a bug fix or rule change happens in one class — not scattered across dozens of controllers, scripts, and API handlers. 09 — Spread the Knowledge Help other developers discover clean Python architecture with DDD.
